name: Ardagh Metal Packaging
desc: Makes aluminium beverage cans for beer, soft drink and energy drink producers from plants in Europe and the Americas.
markets: Can plants and customers in Europe, North America and Brazil; no verified Asia-Pacific operations.
rationale: B2B can supplier to drinks brands; F1 could serve customer hospitality or sustainability messaging, but consumer brand value is low.
changed: Listed on NYSE in 2021 via SPAC merger; majority owned by Ardagh Group

name: Smurfit Westrock
desc: Manufactures corrugated boxes, containerboard, folding cartons and paper-based packaging for consumer goods, retail and industrial customers.
markets: Operations in around 40 countries, mainly across Europe and the Americas, serving brand owners and retailers.
rationale: Large B2B packaging group; F1 hospitality could reach FMCG and retail clients, and sustainability storytelling is possible.
changed: Formed in July 2024 by merger of Smurfit Kappa and WestRock

name: Venture Global
desc: Produces and exports liquefied natural gas from its Calcasieu Pass and Plaquemines plants in Louisiana under long-term contracts.
markets: Exports US LNG to utilities and traders in Europe and Asia; further Louisiana export projects under development.
rationale: B2B LNG exporter selling to utilities; F1 hospitality could support buyer relationships in Europe and Asia, but brand need is limited.
changed: Listed on the NYSE in January 2025

name: Enbridge
desc: Operates crude oil and natural gas pipelines, gas distribution utilities and renewable power assets in Canada and the US.
industry: energy pipeline and gas utility operator
markets: Pipelines and gas utilities across Canada and the United States; no significant operations outside North America.
rationale: Regulated North American infrastructure business with little consumer marketing need; weak F1 fit beyond corporate hospitality.

name: Chart Industries
desc: Designs and makes cryogenic equipment such as storage tanks, heat exchangers and liquefaction systems for LNG, hydrogen and industrial gases.
markets: Sells to energy, industrial gas and chemical customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Engineering equipment brand with hydrogen and LNG technology; F1 B2B hospitality possible, but low marketing culture.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to be acquired by Baker Hughes; completion not confirmed here

name: Vestas Wind Systems
desc: Designs, manufactures, installs and services onshore and offshore wind turbines for utilities and renewable energy developers.
markets: Turbines installed and serviced worldwide, with factories in Europe, the Americas, India, China, Taiwan and Australia.
rationale: Global renewable-energy engineering brand; F1 sustainability agenda and B2B hospitality with utilities could make sense.

name: GardaWorld
desc: Provides security guarding, armoured cash transport, cash management and international protective and risk services to businesses and governments.
markets: Operates in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia for corporate and government clients.
rationale: B2B security group; event security and corporate hospitality offer some F1 relevance, but consumer marketing need is low.
changed: Taken private in 2020; founder Stephan Cretier is a leading shareholder

name: Securitas
desc: Provides security guarding, electronic security, fire and safety, and risk-management services to corporate, industrial and public clients.
markets: Operates in around 45 countries across Europe, North America, Latin America, Asia and Africa.
rationale: Large B2B security brand; event security services and corporate hospitality give some F1 angle, though not consumer-led.

name: Resideo Technologies
desc: Makes Honeywell Home thermostats, First Alert detectors and home security products, and runs ADI security products distribution.
markets: Mainly United States and Canada, with sales and distribution in Europe and other markets.
rationale: Mostly North American home products brand sold via installers; limited F1 fit beyond US race marketing.
changed: Spun off from Honeywell in 2018; announced plan to separate ADI distribution business

name: LCI Industries
desc: Through its Lippert brand, supplies chassis, axles, windows, furniture and other components to RV, trailer and marine manufacturers.
markets: Mainly North American RV and trailer makers and aftermarket, with some operations in Europe.
rationale: Component supplier to RV makers with limited international brand ambition; weak F1 fit.

name: Nielsen
desc: Provides TV, streaming and digital audience measurement and ratings data used by broadcasters, publishers and advertisers.
markets: Audience measurement clients across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Media measurement firm; could pitch as F1 audience and sponsorship-valuation data partner rather than as a brand sponsor.
changed: Taken private in 2022 by an Elliott and Brookfield-led consortium

name: Omnicom Group
desc: Advertising and marketing communications holding group owning agency networks such as BBDO, TBWA, OMD and McCann.
markets: Agencies serve large advertisers in over 100 countries across all major regions.
rationale: Agency group that advises sponsors; F1 relevance is mainly as an intermediary and for B2B hospitality with clients.
changed: Acquired Interpublic Group in 2025

name: Warner Bros. Discovery
desc: Media group owning Warner Bros. studios, HBO, HBO Max streaming, CNN, TNT Sports, Discovery and other networks.
markets: Content, networks and streaming sold across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Major sports and entertainment broadcaster; F1 content, promotion and streaming tie-ins could make commercial sense.
changed: Agreed in 2026 to be acquired by Paramount Skydance; Wikipedia describes WBD as a former company
f1: Parent Paramount Skydance owns Paramount+, a listed F1 partner

name: AppsFlyer
desc: Provides mobile marketing attribution and analytics software that lets app developers and advertisers measure ad campaign performance.
markets: Customers are app businesses and advertisers worldwide, with offices in Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B adtech brand with Israeli roots; F1 could offer technology showcase and client hospitality, but brand reach is narrow.

name: MFE-MediaForEurope
desc: Commercial broadcaster operating free and digital TV channels in Italy, Spain and Germany, funded mainly by advertising.
markets: Television operations in Italy, Spain and, through ProSiebenSat.1, Germany and Austria.
rationale: Large European ad-funded broadcaster; F1 content and cross-promotion could fit, though it sells media rather than buys sponsorship.
changed: Renamed from Mediaset in 2021; took control of ProSiebenSat.1 in 2025

name: Baidu
desc: Operates China's leading search engine plus Ernie AI models, AI cloud services, iQIYI streaming and Apollo Go robotaxis.
markets: Mainly China; Apollo Go robotaxi service expanding to Hong Kong, the Middle East and Europe.
rationale: Chinese AI and autonomous driving brand; F1 could showcase Apollo Go and AI technology during international expansion.

name: Kantar
desc: Provides consumer panels, brand tracking, advertising effectiveness and marketing research data to brands and agencies.
markets: Research clients across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa.
rationale: B2B research firm; F1 relevance lies mainly in sponsorship measurement and client hospitality, not consumer branding.
changed: Majority sold by WPP to Bain Capital in 2019; Kantar Media sold to H.I.G. Capital in 2025

name: Authentic Brands Group
desc: Brand management company that owns consumer, sports and celebrity brands such as Reebok and licenses them to operating partners.
markets: Licensed brands sold through partners and retailers worldwide, across Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Owns sports and lifestyle brands like Reebok; F1 merchandise or brand-building tie-ins could make commercial sense.

name: Disney Streaming
desc: Disney's streaming technology unit that builds and runs video infrastructure for services including Disney+, Hulu and ESPN.
markets: Supports Disney streaming services available across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Internal technology unit with no separate marketing budget; F1 talks would sit with The Walt Disney Company.
changed: Formerly BAMTech Media; renamed Disney Streaming Services in 2018 and Disney Streaming in 2021

name: Monotype
desc: Licenses fonts and typography software, including Helvetica and the MyFonts library, to brands, device makers and developers.
markets: Font licensing customers worldwide, with offices in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Niche B2B design supplier; F1 fit is weak beyond possible typography or brand-design collaborations.
changed: Taken private by HGGC in 2019

name: Etsy
desc: Runs an online marketplace where independent sellers sell handmade, vintage and craft goods to consumers.
markets: Buyers and sellers mainly in the US, UK, Germany, Canada, France and Australia.
rationale: Consumer marketplace with advertising budget; F1 fit is moderate, mainly reaching US and UK audiences.
changed: Sold Elo7 in 2023

name: Taboola
desc: Places sponsored content recommendations and native ads on publisher websites, earning a share of advertiser spend.
markets: Works with publishers and advertisers across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B adtech brand with limited consumer presence; F1 could support client hospitality, but fit is modest.

name: Instacart (Maplebear Inc.)
desc: Runs an online grocery delivery and pickup service partnered with retailers, plus retail advertising and enterprise software.
markets: Customers in the United States and Canada only; no verified expansion beyond North America.
rationale: Strong US consumer brand; F1's US growth and three American races offer some fit, though reach is North America only.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq in 2023

name: Sprinklr
desc: Sells customer experience management software covering social media, marketing, customer service and research to large enterprises.
markets: Enterprise customers across North America, Europe, the Middle East, India and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise software with social listening tools; F1 could serve as technology showcase and B2B hospitality platform.
changed: Listed on the NYSE in 2021

name: Stagwell
desc: Marketing services network owning agencies such as Anomaly and 72andSunny, plus the Harris Poll and marketing software.
markets: Agencies and offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific serving large brands.
rationale: Agency network with sports marketing work; F1 relevance mainly as intermediary or for client hospitality.
changed: Formed through 2021 merger of The Stagwell Group with MDC Partners

name: Roku
desc: Makes the Roku TV operating system and streaming players and earns advertising revenue from The Roku Channel.
markets: Mainly United States, plus Canada, Mexico, Latin America and the UK.
rationale: Consumer streaming brand selling advertising; F1 content and US audience growth give moderate fit.
changed: Wikipedia states Roku, Inc. is now owned by Fox Corporation; not independently confirmed here

name: The Trade Desk
desc: Operates a self-service demand-side platform that agencies and brands use to buy digital advertising across channels.
markets: Agency and advertiser clients in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific through offices worldwide.
rationale: B2B adtech leader; F1 B2B hospitality with agencies and data showcase possible, though consumer brand value is low.

name: Alibaba Group
desc: Runs Taobao and Tmall marketplaces, AliExpress, Alibaba.com, Alibaba Cloud and logistics and local services businesses.
markets: Core business in China, with international commerce and cloud operations across Asia, Europe, the Middle East and Americas.
rationale: Global tech brand with Olympic sponsorship experience; F1 could support Alibaba Cloud and AliExpress international growth.

name: KTM AG
desc: Austrian manufacturer of KTM motorcycles for off-road, street and adventure riding, with a MotoGP racing programme.
markets: Sells motorcycles through dealers across Europe, North America, India and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Motorsport-led brand already in MotoGP and Dakar; F1 audience overlap is strong, though finances were recently restructured.
changed: Bajaj Auto took a controlling stake in 2025 after KTM's 2024-25 insolvency restructuring; Pierer Mobility renamed Bajaj Mobility

name: Soho House
desc: Operates private members' clubs, hotels, restaurants and co-working spaces, earning membership fees and food, drink and room sales.
markets: Clubs in cities across the UK, Europe, North America and Asia, serving affluent members.
rationale: Premium lifestyle brand with affluent audience; F1 hospitality and race-weekend club events could fit well.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to be taken private by an MCR Hotels-led investor group; previously NYSE-listed

name: AC Milan
desc: Italian Serie A football club earning revenue from broadcasting, sponsorship, merchandise and matchday sales at San Siro.
markets: Plays in Italy and Europe, with a worldwide fan base and commercial partners across many regions.
rationale: Sports property selling sponsorship rather than buying it; F1 cross-promotion possible, but it is not a natural sponsor.
changed: Acquired by RedBird Capital Partners from Elliott Management in 2022

name: Tottenham Hotspur
desc: English Premier League football club that also runs the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium for NFL games, concerts and events.
markets: Plays in England and Europe, with a global fan base and international commercial partners.
rationale: Sports property and venue owner; F1 tie-ins such as events or co-marketing possible, but it is not a natural sponsor.
changed: Daniel Levy stepped down as executive chairman in 2025; ENIC remains controlling owner

name: Philips
desc: Makes medical imaging, patient monitoring and sleep and respiratory equipment, plus personal care products such as Sonicare and Avent.
markets: Sells across Europe, North America, China and other Asia-Pacific markets, Latin America and the Middle East.
rationale: Global consumer and health technology brand with sports sponsorship history; F1 could support personal care marketing.
changed: Spun off lighting as Signify and sold its TV and audio businesses
f1: Philips brand licensee PPDS (Philips Professional Displays, owned by TPV) is an F1 partner; not Philips itself

name: Adani Enterprises
desc: Flagship Adani Group company running coal mining and trading, airports, roads, data centres, solar manufacturing and other businesses.
markets: Mainly India, with coal mining in Australia and coal trading across Asia.
rationale: High-profile Indian group already in cricket sponsorship; F1 could support international profile, though reputation risks exist.

name: Intuit
desc: Sells TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma and Mailchimp financial and marketing software to consumers and small businesses.
markets: Mainly United States, with QuickBooks and Mailchimp customers in Canada, the UK, Australia and other markets.
rationale: Heavy US advertiser with sports partnerships; F1's US growth and small-business audience give moderate-to-good fit.
changed: Acquired Credit Karma in 2020 and Mailchimp in 2021

name: Vantage Data Centers
desc: Develops and operates hyperscale data centre campuses that lease capacity to cloud providers and large technology companies.
markets: Campuses in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions for hyperscale cloud customers.
rationale: B2B infrastructure with few customers; F1 offers AI-infrastructure showcase and hospitality, but brand need is limited.

name: Pure Data Centres
desc: Develops and operates large data centre campuses leased to hyperscale cloud providers and other large technology customers.
markets: Data centre campuses in the UK and continental Europe; other expansion not verified here.
rationale: B2B infrastructure brand with few hyperscale customers; weak F1 fit beyond occasional client hospitality.

name: Careem
desc: Runs a super app offering ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery, payments and other services in the Middle East.
markets: Operates in about 10 countries across the Middle East, North Africa and South Asia.
rationale: Strong Gulf consumer brand; F1 races in Abu Dhabi, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Bahrain give clear regional fit.
changed: Uber acquired Careem in 2020; e& took 50.03% of the super app in 2023 while Uber kept ride-hailing

name: Lockton
desc: Privately owned insurance broker providing commercial insurance, employee benefits and risk management advice to businesses.
markets: Offices and clients across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: B2B broker where F1 hospitality could help win corporate clients; consumer brand value is low.

name: Arthur J. Gallagher & Co.
desc: Insurance broker and risk management firm providing brokerage, benefits consulting and claims services to businesses and individuals.
markets: Operations around the world, with major presence in the US, UK, Australia, Canada and other markets.
rationale: B2B broker with existing sports sponsorship; F1 hospitality could support client acquisition in key markets.
changed: Acquired AssuredPartners in 2025

name: Wipro
desc: Provides IT services, consulting, cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and business process outsourcing to large enterprises.
markets: Clients across North America, Europe, India, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Indian IT rivals sponsor sport and F1 teams; F1 could serve technology showcase and enterprise hospitality.

name: WTW
desc: Provides insurance broking, risk advisory, employee benefits, retirement and investment consulting to companies and institutions.
markets: Clients in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions through offices in many countries.
rationale: B2B advisory brand; F1 hospitality could support corporate client relationships, but consumer fit is weak.
changed: Formed by merger of Willis Group and Towers Watson in 2016

name: Odoo
desc: Develops open-source business software covering accounting, CRM, inventory, e-commerce and HR, sold by subscription to SMEs.
markets: SME customers and partners worldwide across Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Fast-growing SME software brand with sports sponsorship history; F1 could build international brand awareness.
changed: Renamed from OpenERP, originally TinyERP, in 2014

name: Sompo Holdings
desc: Japanese insurance group providing property and casualty, life and specialty insurance, plus nursing care services.
markets: Mainly Japan, with Sompo International specialty insurance in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Major Japanese insurer with sports sponsorship history; F1 Japanese Grand Prix and international specialty business give some fit.
changed: Acquired Aspen Insurance in 2025

name: Ingram Micro
desc: Distributes IT hardware, software and cloud services to resellers and managed service providers, with logistics services.
markets: Operations in many countries across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B distributor; F1 hospitality could support vendor and reseller relationships, though consumer brand value is low.
changed: Acquired by Platinum Equity in 2021; relisted on the NYSE in 2024

name: Quest Global
desc: Provides engineering design, development and manufacturing engineering services to aerospace, automotive, energy, medical and industrial clients.
markets: Operates more than 100 locations in 17 countries serving clients across Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Engineering services firm; F1 could showcase engineering capability to aerospace and automotive clients, though brand awareness is low.

name: Remy Cointreau
desc: Produces and sells premium spirits including Remy Martin and Louis XIII cognac, Cointreau liqueur and The Botanist gin.
markets: Sells mainly in the United States, China and Europe, with distribution across Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Luxury spirits brand where rivals sponsor F1; hospitality and premium positioning fit, subject to alcohol advertising rules.

name: Unit4
desc: Sells cloud ERP, financial management and HR software to professional services, education, public sector and non-profit organisations.
markets: Offices in 23 countries across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: Mid-sized B2B software vendor in services sectors; modest F1 fit beyond client hospitality.
changed: Majority acquired by TA Associates in 2021

name: Atos
desc: Provides IT services, managed infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity and digital transformation to companies and governments.
markets: Clients in Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Former Olympic IT partner with sports-technology experience; F1 fit limited by its recent financial restructuring.
changed: Completed financial restructuring in 2024 and sold several business units

name: Legal & General
desc: Provides pensions, annuities, life insurance, lifetime mortgages and investment management to individuals and institutions.
markets: Mainly UK, with asset management and pension risk transfer business in the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Well-known UK financial brand; F1 audience overlaps with affluent customers, though most business is UK-focused.
changed: Sold its US protection business to Meiji Yasuda in 2025

name: Brightline
desc: Operates higher-speed intercity passenger trains between Miami and Orlando and is developing a Las Vegas-California line.
markets: Passenger services in Florida only; Brightline West between Las Vegas and Southern California under development.
rationale: Florida-only rail operator; Miami Grand Prix and planned Las Vegas service give local co-marketing angle.

name: Concentrix
desc: Provides outsourced customer experience services, contact centres and related technology for large companies across many industries.
markets: Operates in over 70 countries across Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: B2B service provider with large scale; F1 fit limited to client hospitality and technology showcase.
changed: Spun off from SYNNEX in 2020; merged with Webhelp in 2023

name: Ayvens
desc: Provides long-term vehicle leasing, fleet management and car subscription services to companies and individuals, and sells used cars.
markets: Direct presence in about 42 countries, mainly Europe, plus Latin America and Asia.
rationale: Leasing brand linked to automotive; F1 could support corporate fleet hospitality and brand building in Europe.
changed: Formed in 2023 from ALD Automotive's acquisition of LeasePlan
